Series::frac¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::frac() const -> Series
Series& Series::frac_()

What It Does¶

frac() returns the fractional part of each value, defined as

frac(x) = x - floor(x)

Because it subtracts floor() (which rounds toward negative infinity), the result is always in [0, 1), even for negative inputs:

  • frac(1.25) = 0.25

  • frac(-1.25) = 0.75 — not -0.25

  • frac(3.0) = 0.0

That is the “sawtooth” fractional part: it rises linearly from 0 to just below 1 and drops back to 0 at every integer. It is the tool for wrapping a continuous coordinate into a unit cell — texture coordinates, phase into one period, a position into [0, 1).

frac() requires a floating-point input.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series or Series& x - floor(x), always in [0, 1). frac_() overwrites the current storage.

Gradient¶

frac() is differentiable, with derivative 1 between the integer jumps:

d/dx frac(x) = 1

floor(x) is locally constant, so subtracting it does not change the slope. The jump at each integer is a measure-zero set and is not represented in the gradient.

Examples¶

Example 1. The fractional part is always non-negative, including for negatives.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({1.25, -1.25, 3.0, -0.75}).frac());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[0.2500, 0.7500, 0.0000, 0.2500]

-1.25 - floor(-1.25) = -1.25 - (-2) = 0.75, and -0.75 - (-1) = 0.25.

Example 2. The gradient is 1 everywhere the function is smooth.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.25, 2.75, 3.5});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

x.frac().sum().reverse();

std::cout << "dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 1, 1]

Example 3. frac() is floating-point only, because it is built on floor().

try {
  pluss::make_series({1, 2, 3}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64).frac();
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

floor: dtype not implemented

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • frac() uses floor(), so the result of a negative input is its distance above the next lower integer, not x - trunc(x). frac(-1.25) is 0.75, not -0.25.

  • Integer input raises (the error names floor). Convert to a floating-point dtype first.

  • NaN propagates.

Summary¶

frac(x) is the sawtooth fractional part x - floor(x):

  • always in [0, 1), including for negatives

  • floating-point input only

  • differentiable, derivative 1 between integer jumps

See Also¶

  • Series::floor: the piece subtracted off; x = floor(x) + frac(x).

  • Series::trunc: rounds toward zero instead, giving a signed fractional part when subtracted.

  • Series::remainder: frac(x) is remainder(x, 1.0).
